dial.summary: 4/8 indicators supportive on November 16 — perp funding rates flipped slightly negative (-0.0004%) with Fear & Greed at 11 (Extreme Fear), signaling deleveraged capitulation and a classic accumulation zone; ISM Manufacturing at 55.5 (10th consecutive expansion) and Global M2 at $104.3T sustain the macro bid; DXY at 103.42 (above 100 threshold, headwind) is the primary drag; next key catalysts are the Nov 25 Oct PCE print, the Dec 1 ISM Manufacturing release, and the December 9 FOMC decision.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 aggregate (US/Euro Zone/China/Japan) at ~$104.3T as of September 2026 (104,317.08B per MacroMicro series); October G4 data not yet published as of November 16, 2026 — typically updated mid-to-late November following the reference month; broader global M2 estimate from Bitrue: $103.66T, Au79 Macro cited $103.89T (wider aggregates than G4); US M2 $23.41T in Sep 2026 (+5.7% YoY per FRED H.6, next release Nov 24); 4-week Aug→Sep G4 change: +$0.64T (+0.6%), above flat threshold — trend UP; status supportive (4-week G4 trend up, no YoY contraction); held unchanged pending October G4 publication.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: October 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.5% (released November 2, 2026), beating consensus 54.7%, up 1.0pp from September's 54.5%; 10th consecutive expansion month; Production sub-index 59.0 (highest since Nov 2021), New Orders 55.5, Employment 52.4; Prices Paid fell to 75.2 from September's 77.9, though input price pressures remain elevated; 4-week trend UP (Sep 54.5 → Oct 55.5, +1.0pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising); next ISM Manufacturing release December 1, 2026 (November data); held unchanged as of November 16 — October 55.5 is the current monthly reading.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot 103.42 as of Monday November 16, 2026 (FXStreet: 103.42, +0.01% on the day; Trading Economics: 103.412, +0.23% daily; prior close Nov 13: 103.28); 4-week trend UP — from ~101.5–101.8 on October 14 to 103.42 on November 16, net +~1.6–1.9%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; hot October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10 release) and hawkish Fed repricing drove the DXY push; Fed Chair Warsh speech today (November 16) is a live catalyst — Fed's Schmid said inflation 'running too hot' this morning; status headwind (DXY above 100 — must fall below 97.5 for supportive); FRED DTWEXBGS network-restricted — ICE spot corroborated via FXStreet and Trading Economics.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield (DFII10) at 2.86% on November 12, 2026 (FRED series; latest available — Nov 13 showed '.' no print, Nov 14–15 weekend, Nov 16 release pending at time of run); recent readings: Nov 6: 2.63%, Nov 9: 2.66%, Nov 10: 2.78%, Nov 12: 2.86%; 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately 2.85–2.90% on October 14 (Oct 5 high 2.95%) to 2.86% on November 12, net change ~0 to -4bps within flat threshold; status neutral (above 2% but flat trend — headwind requires BOTH rising trend AND above 2%); 52-week range 1.72%–2.95%; held at 2.86% pending Nov 16 DFII10 print.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: 2s10s spread at approximately +25bps as of November 12, 2026 (Treasury par yields: 10Y 4.98%, 2Y 4.73%; prior readings: Nov 6: +35bps, Nov 5: +38bps — spread has narrowed as 2Y repriced harder than 10Y on hot CPI); 4-week trend FLAT — from approximately +28–32bps on October 14 to +25bps on November 12, net change approximately -3 to -7bps within flat threshold; status neutral (positive spread, no sustained steepening, not deeply inverted — headwind requires < -50bps); no fresh Nov 13–16 data available at time of run; December 9 FOMC decision will be the next key inflection for 2Y repricing.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,758,867M ($6.759T) for week ended November 11, 2026 (H.4.1 released November 12, 2026; +$10,722M WoW from Nov 4's $6,748,145M, +$178,405M YoY); prior weekly readings: Nov 4 $6,748,145M, Oct 28 $6,745,635M, Oct 21 $6,753,604M, Oct 14 $6,755,639M; 4-week change Oct 14 → Nov 11: +$3,228M (~+$3.2B, essentially flat); balance sheet stabilized post-QT-pause (QT ended December 2025); YoY +$178.4B (+2.7%); status supportive (flat with slight growth, no aggressive QT); next H.4.1 release November 19, 2026 (covering week ended November 18); held at $6.76T pending that release.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass BTC perp funding rate -0.0004% per 8h (~-0.45% annualized) as of November 16, 2026 (OI-weighted, flipped negative from 0.0028–0.0029% on Nov 15); BTC price ~$64.6–65K; CoinGlass futures page: open interest ~$41.91B, 24h liquidations $106.46M (mostly shorts: $68.49M vs $37.98M longs); funding negative on Binance, OKX, Bybit, Gate, and Bitget; Fear & Greed Index at 11 (Extreme Fear); 30-day trend FLAT — mid-October rates were near zero/slightly negative (consistent with current -0.0004%), no sustained directional move; status supportive (well below 0.04% headwind threshold; slightly negative funding combined with Extreme Fear is a textbook accumulation signal); prior cycle peak of 0.0083% on Nov 14 fully flushed out.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$284.9B as of November 15–16, 2026 (DefiLlama; USDT $175.4B, USDC $69.3B, USDT dominance within stables ~61.55%); stablecoin supply has fallen ~$15B over the last 30 days (from ~$300B); BTC.D at ~59.3%, BTC at ~$64.6–65K; implied TOTAL crypto market cap ~$2.28T (BTC mktcap ~$1.36T / 0.593); implied stablecoin dominance ~12.5% ($284.9B / $2.28T); 30-day trend UP — October 14 dominance ~10.5–10.8%, November 16 ~12.5%, net +~1.7–2.0pp; status neutral — headwind requires rising dominance AND rising TOTAL simultaneously; TOTAL has contracted from ~$2.6T (Oct 14) to ~$2.28T so headwind condition not met; supportive condition (falling 30-day dominance) also not met; rising dominance reflects risk-off repositioning during BTC pullback.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts (October 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases October 2026 New Residential Construction at 8:30 AM ET; elevated mortgage rates (30Y near 7.1%) and real yields at 2.86% (historically elevated) continue to pressure housing affordability; a sharp drop in permits would underscore the housing drag on Q4 2026 growth ahead of the Nov 25 PCE print.

upcoming.title: FOMC Minutes — October 27–28 Meeting
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve releases minutes of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting at 2:00 PM ET; the Fed held at 3.75%–4.00% at that meeting; minutes will reveal member views on the December 9 hike threshold given elevated ISM Prices Paid and Iran-war supply shocks; both October CPI (+0.4% MoM, Nov 10) and October PPI (Nov 13) arrived after the October meeting — markets will read the minutes against the new inflation reality; FOMC blackout period begins ~November 29 ahead of the December 9 decision.

upcoming.title: Pending Home Sales (October 2026)
upcoming.note: NAR releases October 2026 Pending Home Sales Index; leading indicator of existing home sales with a 1–2 month lag; elevated rates near 7.1% and real yields at 2.86% are suppressing contract signings; a persistent decline below prior-year levels would confirm housing as a sustained drag on Q4 2026 economic activity.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended November 15, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL releases weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET on Thursday November 19; key weekly labor read ahead of the Thanksgiving-week data lull and the ~November 29 FOMC blackout period; a sustained trend above 220K would add dovish counter-pressure to the December 9 hike case; next NFP release is December 4 (November data), arriving just 5 days before the December 9 FOMC decision.

upcoming.title: Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (November 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia releases November 2026 Manufacturing Business Outlook Survey at 8:30 AM ET; first-look at November manufacturing activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a positive print above 0 would reinforce the October ISM signal at 55.5; released on the third Thursday of the month, same day as jobless claims.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMIs (November 2026)
upcoming.note: S&P Global releases flash estimates for US Manufacturing and Services PMIs for November 2026 at 9:45 AM ET; first real-time read on November business activity ahead of the December 1 ISM Manufacturing PMI; a Services print above 55 would reinforce the sticky-inflation narrative heading into the December 9 FOMC decision; ISM Manufacturing has been at 55.5 for October (10th straight expansion).
